statusDetail: The requested URL redirects to https://www.5movierulz.vote/. All 58 catalog checks were judged. The search path itself returned a 403 bot challenge, recorded as an issue rather than an audit blocker because the other representative templates remained inspectable.

paths.description: Entry page and primary catalogue template; tested desktop, 360px mobile, 780px tablet, dark, reduced-motion and increased-contrast conditions.
Telugu featured category representing listing/archive templates.
Vadala movie page representing the content/detail template; playback/download actions were not activated.
Invalid route representing HTTP error and recovery behaviour.

findings.summary: The site is hard-coded to one dark palette rather than following the user’s colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no color-scheme declaration and no prefers-color-scheme rule; light and dark captures are pixel-identical.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide light/dark design tokens selected with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly with no View Transitions enhancement.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition-name or @view-transition rule across the homepage, listing and detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-origin cross-document View Transitions with a reduced-motion-safe fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no position-aware header or progress feedback.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 7,383 CSS px tall at mobile, while CSS/probe inspection found no scroll-state query, progress indicator or shrinking sticky header.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lightweight scroll-position feedback where it helps orientation, using scroll-state/container queries or declarative scroll progress.

findings.summary: Dropdown menus use brittle absolute positioning rather than anchored, fallback-aware placement.
findings.evidence: CSS uses position:absolute; top:37px; left:0 for nested menus and contains no anchor-name, position-anchor or position-try.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks, retaining a conventional positioned fallback for older browsers.

findings.summary: An invisible full-viewport advertising link overlays the page and can intercept user interaction.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified body.home > a#dontfoid as a fixed 412×823 link to digital.ppwpn.com with no accessible name; the page probe independently counted a full-viewport overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the click-capture ad overlay. Any advertising must be visibly labelled, bounded, non-blocking and user-initiated.

findings.summary: The full-page interruption is an unnamed ad-hoc anchor with no dismiss mechanism.
findings.evidence: The overlay is a fixed <a id="dontfoid">, not a dialog/popover, has no accessible name and covers the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete the overlay; for legitimate transient UI use popover or dialog with explicit labelling and light-dismiss/close behaviour.

findings.summary: Navigation and repeated sidebar chrome delay the content, especially on mobile.
findings.evidence: The 360px capture spends roughly the first 430px on branding, search and a ten-item menu before content; listing/detail templates repeat large category/year sidebars.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary taxonomy navigation behind an accessible disclosure and prioritise the page’s title and content in the first viewport.

findings.summary: The layout overflows horizontally at tablet widths.
findings.evidence: At a 780×800 viewport the layout primitive reported scrollWidth 1002px and 222px horizontal overflow; the 769–1024px media-query block is empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the fixed 1000px wrapper with fluid/max-inline-size layout and cover the tablet range with intrinsic sizing.

findings.summary: Reusable cards and navigation adapt only through global viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container rules or container-type declarations on any representative template.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable movie grids/cards and navigation where the same component appears in different widths.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is hidden, dropdowns are hover-only, and many links have very small targets.
findings.evidence: Focused navigation links computed to outline:none/0px; dropdown CSS has :hover but no :focus-within and no aria-expanded; probes found at least 30 visible targets under 24px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore strong :focus-visible styling, make menus operable by keyboard/touch, and enlarge targets toward 44×44 CSS px.

findings.summary: The primary search journey is blocked by a bot challenge.
findings.evidence: Navigating to ?s=Vadala returned HTTP 403 and a Cloudflare “Verify you are human” page instead of results.
findings.suggestedFix: Tune bot protection so ordinary search navigation is not challenged; provide a server-rendered results fallback and a recoverable challenge path.

findings.summary: Search failure offers no site-level recovery, while the 404 fallback points to an inconsistent host.
findings.evidence: The search route exposes only Cloudflare verification; the 404 page’s search action targets www.5movierulz.house while the canonical site is .vote.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep recovery controls on the canonical host, preserve the query, and provide retry/back/home options when verification or search fails.

findings.summary: The page eagerly loads every below-fold poster and incurs an avoidable host redirect.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 47 requests/562KB and a 301 from .legal to .vote; image audit found 28 below-fold images without loading="lazy" and 32/32 without srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the canonical host directly, lazy-load below-fold images, add responsive sources and prioritise only the LCP image.

findings.summary: Advertising and analytics scripts dominate transferred JavaScript.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 166KB to Google Tag Manager and about 67KB to acscdn scripts; eight analytics collection requests fire on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate analytics destinations and defer or eliminate ad scripts that do not provide proportional user value.

findings.summary: Key controls and document structures lack accessible names or valid semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found the full-page ad link has no discernible name and three list items have invalid parents; the search input has neither label nor aria-label and pages have no <main>.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the overlay, label the search input, use valid list/landmark structure and expose one main landmark.

findings.summary: Several text links on the detail template fail minimum colour contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse detail reported six color-contrast failures and three link-in-text-block failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust muted/link colours to meet WCAG AA and distinguish inline links by more than colour alone.

findings.summary: Focus is invisible on navigation and heading/landmark structure is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus on HOME/FEATURED computed outline:none; there is no main landmark, and the detail template introduces a second H1 for “Posts navigation”.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible :focus-visible styles, one main landmark, one page-level H1 and a logical heading hierarchy.

findings.summary: Tablet reflow and target sizing do not meet an inclusive input/zoom baseline.
findings.evidence: The tablet layout has 222px overflow, and many text links are only 14–16px high; viewport scaling is not disabled and no embedded media was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use fluid reflow and enlarge interactive target boxes without disabling zoom.

findings.summary: Poster images are forcibly displayed at the wrong aspect ratio.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 32 image-aspect-ratio failures on home; 165×220 sources were displayed at approximately 176×200.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve intrinsic aspect ratio with height:auto/aspect-ratio and generate correctly sized responsive variants.

findings.summary: The detail template uses a deprecated API and blocks BFCache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse detail reported one deprecation warning and one BFCache failure reason.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the deprecated API and the unload/BFCache blocker identified in the Lighthouse artifact.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are inconsistent: there is no sitemap and the 404 page asks to be indexed.
findings.evidence: /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404; the real 404 response emits robots=index,follow and a self-referencing canonical.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap, set 404 pages to noindex, and keep canonical/robots signals consistent with status codes.

findings.summary: Movie entities have Open Graph tags but no structured data.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found og:type=video.movie and a preview image, but zero JSON-LD blocks.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org Movie JSON-LD matching the visible title, image, director, cast and synopsis.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but core transport and XSS hardening headers are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no CSP, HSTS or X-Content-Type-Options; no cookies or mixed-content issue was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP, HSTS and nosniff header while retaining secure cookie defaults.

findings.summary: The page loads a broad advertising/tracking footprint before user action.
findings.evidence: Tracker audit found seven third-party origins including Google Analytics/GTM, adexchangerapid.com and usrpubtrk.com; eight analytics calls fire and the ad script injects a click-capture overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential ad trackers, consolidate analytics, obtain meaningful consent where required and load optional third parties only after that choice.

findings.summary: Most browser-enforced defensive policies are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no HSTS, CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or nosniff; X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN was the only listed defence present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, CSP with frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and nosniff, staged in report-only where appropriate.

findings.summary: Third-party runtime code can insert a viewport-sized, unnamed interaction layer.
findings.evidence: The ad overlay is fixed over the viewport and injected by third-party advertising code, making navigation behaviour dependent on fragile external runtime code.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove click-capture injection and isolate optional third parties so core navigation remains deterministic.

findings.summary: A multilingual movie catalogue is not prepared for alternate writing directions.
findings.evidence: Pages declare lang=en-US, but CSS inspection found no logical inline/block properties and no dir handling across templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical CSS properties and ensure language/direction can be set per localized page or content segment.

findings.summary: The invisible full-page advertising link is a disguised, deceptive interaction target.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse shows an unnamed fixed link to an advertising domain covering the entire 412×823 viewport, so a user can trigger an ad without choosing a visible ad.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the click-capture overlay and keep every sponsored link visible, labelled and bounded to its ad creative.

findings.summary: All poster images use legacy JPEG without responsive sources or lazy loading.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 32 legacy-format images, zero modern-format images, 32 without srcset and 28 below-fold images loaded eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, add srcset/sizes and lazy-load offscreen posters.

findings.summary: Duplicate analytics and advertising work runs on every page load.
findings.evidence: Eight Google Analytics collection requests plus multiple ad/tracking beacons fire during a simple content-page load.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate analytics to one necessary destination and defer optional tracking/ads until needed and permitted.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts consume a disproportionate share of this otherwise simple page.
findings.evidence: Of 562KB transferred, GTM accounts for 166KB and acscdn ad scripts about 67KB; the page itself has no video/audio payload to justify this overhead.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget and remove or defer scripts that do not deliver direct user value.
